assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Becomes red if the choice were the minimum expected score, if the max selection were inverted, or if expected were keyed by candidate index rather than member id; the scores are authored in the test, not read back.

assertion_analysis.assertion: on an all-equal judged score of 0.7, choice == "beta"
assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Becomes red if the tie-break drops select_anchor and falls to bare id order, which would return "alpha" (the minimum id).
Becomes red if the placeholder-description member or the missing-documentation member is offered to the judge.

assertion_analysis.assertion: calls == [] and choice is None for a family of ineligible members
assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Becomes red if a call is made for a family with no eligible member, or if an empty family fabricates a default choice.

assertion_analysis.assertion: choice is None and expected == {} when every call fails
assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Becomes red if a failed call is read as a zero score or replaced by a default anchor.
Becomes red if one failed member discards the whole family's scored result.

assertion_analysis.assertion: state["house_style_template"] == TEMPLATE_MARKER recorded in the state
assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Becomes red when the template key is dropped from the state; this is the declared negative control (negative_control.log, EXIT=1).

assertion_analysis.assertion: asked == ("base_quantity", "child") with the parent folded in
assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Becomes red if a parent not already present in members is not offered as a candidate.

assertion_analysis.assertion: the real accessor returns "Opening.\nA shared note.\nSecond opening."
assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Becomes red if the helper reads a different registry key, drops the note, or reorders; it exercises the real _house_style_template, not the stub.

findings.text: follow-on: the house-style template is looked up by name through conventions_context_for(pattern_name), but the argument is str(parent_id or candidates[0]["id"]); when a real parent node id is present and is not itself a parseable standard name the accessor returns None on ParseError and the state's house_style_template is silently empty for a family whose members would parse, so the judge is asked without the house-style template the question cites, and no test covers that empty path.

follow-on: the tie-break calls select_anchor(None, None, None, tied), passing None for the parent so the heuristic's rule 1 cannot fire; the docstring two lines below claims the judged choice never contradicts the heuristic on equal evidence, which does not hold when an accepted parent ties at the top, where select_anchor would return the parent outright and this does not.

follow-on: assert question["criteria"] == list(families.TEMPLATE_FITNESS_LEVELS) compares the returned criteria against the same module constant the function builds them from, so the two sides move together and the assertion only restates the implementation; it constrains no behaviour the level text depends on, and the adjacent length check at line 224 is the only independent half.
